status: declared by the pull request that closes #1360 before any score was computed; a development study, never a verdict. B4 is a benchmark of the registered test that Eleonora asked for (2 November 2026, chat, relayed on #1360), added beside B1, B1' and B2. Nothing is registered or published: no record in docs/runs/ is edited, the live record and its pin do not change, the candidate (s3c-ann-net) does not change, docs/research/h5-candidate.json is not changed, and no declaration already merged is changed. Whether B4 joins the protocol's decision rule or is reported beside it is a marked question for Eleonora in the pull request (default: reported beside, B1 stays the deciding benchmark); this declaration settles nothing on it
hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Registration design, step 4 to 5. Development tier
ruling: Eleonora, 2 November 2026, chat, relayed on #1360, after an outside publication-readiness review: add a plain quantile regression on reserves and calendar days as a benchmark in the registered test, beside B1, B1' and B2
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)
why: A referee will ask whether the candidate beats a parsimonious model that reads the same public reserve and calendar information. B1 (persistence), B1' (calendar-aware persistence) and B2 (climatology) each read one of those and not the others. Linear quantile models exist in earlier studies (docs/pivot/conditional-vs-climatology-holdout.md, settlement-timing-result.md) but not on the protocol's common grid against the current candidate
decision_instant: 18:00 America/New_York on the decision day (repo_model.decision_instant.DECISION_TIME, amended on 29 October 2026, #1312). Every walk of this study, the references included, is made at that instant

b4.name: B4
b4.model: for each lead h = 1..5 and each level tau of the protocol's grid (scoring_protocol.GRID, 23 levels) one linear quantile regression of spread_bps on the target day, in bp, on: an intercept; the last observed spread (the spread of the as-of anchor, bp); the as-of reserve measure (reserve_balances, USD trillion); and the calendar terms below, read at the target day
b4.last_observed_spread: spread_bps of the as-of anchor, the last row public at the decision instant (protocol_benchmarks._anchor), the same row B1 reads

reserve_measure.column: reserve_balances, the panel column that the reserves leg of the scarcity state (repo_model.scarcity) and gbm_funding read, in USD trillion (the panel's USD billion over 1000)
reserve_measure.read: as of the decision instant, per field, by repo_model.asof.InformationRule (metadata/sources.json availability), horizon 1: the value of the latest row on which reserve_balances was public at the decision. A training pair is trained on the value read at its own decision day (the row h before its target); a forecast reads the value of its own decision day. A row after the decision is refused with LookAheadError (b4_quantile_regression.read_reserves)
reserve_measure.why_not_the_scarcity_state: the scarcity state of #115 (0 abundant to 3 scarce, repo_model.scarcity.own_leg_states) is unknown on every 2026 development day (169 days from 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-02 in the measurement panel built from the tracked fixtures, found in the preparation of this declaration), so a benchmark on it could not be scored on the 2026 days. The reserves column is public throughout. Whether to read the state or a ratio in place of the level is a marked question in the pull request
reserve_measure.unknown: a pair whose reserve value is unknown is dropped from the fit; a decision whose reserve value is unknown has no B4 forecast and the study refuses it (the walk raises). The count of dropped pairs is kept in each estimate

calendar_terms.terms: month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement_coupon, settlement_bill, dom_19_23 and post_month_end_window: spread_mr_calendar.NO_FOMC_IORB, the terms of the candidate's base (s3), as 0/1 flags of the TARGET row read by spread_mr_calendar.TermTable
calendar_terms.read_at_the_target_day: a flag is read from the target row (the calendar columns, known in advance) on direct pairs; a scheduled field (settlement_coupon, settlement_bill: treasury_settlement_*) is read only where asof rule 2 admits it, which is lead 1 (spread_mr_calendar.readable_offsets, TermTable.read); at leads 2 to 5 those two terms are not in the fit. B4 does not read the auction-announcement dating of the candidate (s3c_announced, #1288): that is the candidate's addition, not a plain calendar column, and it is a stated difference between B4 and the candidate
calendar_terms.not_included: fomc_day and iorb_window (the candidate's base leaves them out, #1196, #1145)
calendar_terms.enters: a term enters a lead's fit only if at least spread_mr_calendar.MIN_FLAGGED (3) training pairs carry its flag, as in the candidate's fits

b4.training_pairs: direct. For the decision on row D with anchor A and lag L = D - A, and lead h, a training pair has target row T in [h + L, A] and decision row T - h; the pair is spread_mean_reversion.training_rows' pair (origin = T - (h + L), the anchor row of the pair's decision row T - h). Its regressors are the last spread (spread_bps of the origin), the reserve value read at the pair's decision row, and the flags of T at lead h; its response is spread_bps of T. Every row read is at or before the anchor (protocol_benchmarks._require_public, LookAheadError). The fitter b4_quantile_regression.fit_quantile_regression carries @guard_one_step_fit, takes training_pairs = 'direct' only and needs no entry in repo_model.one_step_guard.ONE_STEP_ALLOW_LIST (which is not changed)
b4.window: expanding: every direct pair from the first panel row to the anchor (the candidate's own fits use the trailing two years; the directive asks for an expanding window for B4). A fit needs at least spread_mean_reversion.MIN_PAIRS (60) pairs at every lead; otherwise the decision has no forecast
b4.refit: every spread_mean_reversion.REFIT_EVERY (21) decision days from the first scored decision day of the window, the candidate's cadence (spread_mr_state_calendar.walk); between refits the coefficients are kept and the last observed spread, the reserve value and the flags of the target are read afresh

estimator.loss: the check loss of tau, summed over the training pairs, plus RIDGE times the sum of squared non-intercept coefficients; the intercept is not penalised
estimator.ridge_units: the coefficients are in bp per bp (last spread), bp per USD trillion (reserves) and bp per flagged day, so the penalty is of the order of one pseudo-day on a flag; it is the one fixed ridge of the directive and nothing is tuned
estimator.solver: iteratively reweighted least squares on the check loss (a quadratic majorizer of |r| at the previous residual, weight 1 / (2 max(|r|, EPSILON))), solved by ridge-penalised normal equations, started from the ridge least-squares fit at the first level and from the previous level's coefficients after that; EPSILON = 0.001 bp; at most 100 iterations; stops when no coefficient moves by more than 1e-6. The levels are fitted in increasing order. Stdlib only, so the benchmark reproduces with no install
estimator.non_crossing: the 23 fitted quantiles at each lead are sorted (the rearrangement of Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val and Galichon), so the scorer, which refuses a crossing, accepts them; the number of forecasts the sort changed is counted
estimator.no_tuning: ridge, EPSILON, the iteration cap, MIN_FLAGGED and MIN_PAIRS are fixed here. No variant of B4 is scored; B4 is scored once

b4.protocol_benchmarks: repo_model.protocol_benchmarks.b4_forecast(panel, decision_index, *, registry, decision_time, splits, ...) is B4's forecast of one decision, refitted at that decision (the live record and the registration can score it by day); the walk of this study, b4_quantile_regression.walk, refits every 21 decision days as the candidate does. The B4 of the two functions is the same fit on the same decision day, which a test pins

references.name: sc_s3c_ann_net
references.label: (s3c-ann-net)
references.role: the H5 candidate; re-walked at 18:00 in the same run with #1288's and #1356's machinery, unchanged

references.name: B1
references.label: B1
references.role: protocol benchmark B1, the deciding benchmark

frame.windows: the two windows of #1255, loaded as #1255 loads them: the development window (decision days whose five targets fall on or before 2025-12-31) and the 2026 development days (targets 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03, the near-blind tier open since GO #151). The 2026 days are shown apart, as a window, and decide nothing. No locked day and no day after 2026-09-03 is scored; the frames' own guards refuse them
frame.days: B4 is walked over exactly the decision days of the frame; a scored decision day without a B4 forecast is refused, so every model is compared on the same days
frame.reproduction: (s3c-ann-net) is walked as scripts/s3c_ann_net_cmb_1356.py walks its reference at 18:00; its pooled means in this run must agree with docs/research/s3c-ann-net-cmb-1356/result.json to 1e-9 or the study stops

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as in docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md, reported beside
primary.calibration: the coverage of the central 90% band (q5 to q95, closed) of every model, pooled and by lead; a rate, reported as a mean and not tested

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1360, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.comparisons: B4 against B1, B1' and B2 (does the plain model beat the benchmarks it joins), and the candidate against B4, B1, B1' and B2 (does the candidate beat each). d = score of the reference less score of the candidate, so positive favours the candidate of the row
scoring.splits: pooled; by lead; by regime; by pressure-day type; by calendar day type of the target (scripts/srf_cap_1241.py and #1115's groups, as #1255 loads them); a group with fewer than the frame's minimum days is listed and not tested
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): the row is read better when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, and undecided otherwise. A point estimate alone is not read

reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; the candidate stays (s3c-ann-net).
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and day-type splits beside it.
Where B4 beats the candidate in a split, the page says so plainly; it is what the benchmark is for.
Whether B4 joins the decision rule is Eleonora's, as a marked question with numbered options and a default that changes no claim (reported beside; B1 stays the deciding benchmark).

limits.candidate: unchanged; no candidate arm, term or walk is edited
limits.sources: metadata/sources.json, docs/decisions/information-set.md and docs/decisions/scoring-protocol.md are not changed; the decision rule of the protocol is not changed; docs/runs/ is not touched
limits.register: no gradient-boosted fitter is called, so the provisional register's producer table is unaffected; the declaration reads calendar columns on direct pairs and has a cleared row (metadata/provisional/cleared/b4_quantile_regression_1360.json)

long_run: cloud first. Measured on a subset before the full run; if the full run is expected to exceed about two hours it goes to the Mac as a `needs-mac:` comment with the exact commands
